pr_title: eth/downloader: move the pivot in beacon sync mode too
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/26429.

In legacy (pre-merge) sync mode, headers were contiguously downloaded from the network and when no more headers were available, we checked every few seconds whether there are 64 new blocks to move the pivot.

In beacon (post-merge) sync mode, we don't need to check for new skeleton headers non stop, since those re delivered one by one by the engine API. The missing code snippet from the header fetcher was to actually look at the latest head and move the pivot if it was more than 2*64-8 away. This PR adds the missing movement logic.

The convoluted logic of pulling headers from disk if they don't exist in the skeleton chain shouldn't really be needed, but I've added it as a sanity check in case I'm missing some reasoning now. It should result in a warning anyway so we can investigate if that clause is actually triggered.

## This PR

Some charts
![Screenshot 2023-01-10 at 09-06-08 Single Geth - Grafana](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/142290/211495611-bc655fc2-929f-4220-a016-16402dc5f0c4.png)

This is _this_ PR. IT has a fairly stable ingress rate for the duration of the sync. 

## Master

Here's master: 
![Screenshot 2023-01-10 at 09-06-41 Single Geth - Grafana](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/142290/211495917-995c05bf-af9e-4161-904a-1b238dcb59fd.png)

As you can see, the snap traffic comes if fits and bursts - not quite like the report in https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/26429 , where it's totally dead for the duration of the block downloads. The reason for this is [this](https://github.com/holiman/factor/commit/73fd240934d784f350fe925e289e71df8c29b695) change in factor , which made factor check new heads less often. Because of this, there's a higher chance that factor misses a head, and thus that geth notices a `gapped beaconchain`. When geth detects a beacon gap, the sync is restarted. 

And restarting the sync is similar to moving the pivot.

The TL;DR is that once the block download phase finished, it does 5 pivot movements with a few seconds in between. 16,240,072 -> 16,242,137 , 2065 blocks, representing nearly 7 hours.


This is because head updates from the CL node does not trigger pivot movements, only full block download does. But if our head pivot is already at 16M, and we spend 6 hours downloading `16M -> genesis`, then obviously nothing will push it. 

This needs to be fixed by somehow trigger pivot movements from head updates.

review_comments:
Actually it's possible to happen(new pivot point is still in local)

For example:

- current remote head is 101
- current local head is 99
- skeleton header chain range is [100, 101]
- current pivot point is `101-64=37`
- start sync
- new remote head becomes 158
- `158-37 > 2*64-8`, pivot point moves
- new pivot point becomes 94
- new pivot point is still in range of local chain

If I leave some nitpicks, is that the local chain part is already resolved previously which can be reused, https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/26453/files#diff-8cb29165929b2bd4c8f7c019a95cc8a69d3e36320703308f5c835fa97bdd8f31R288

But I think it's fine. Just a very very special corner case.
@rjl493456442 do you have any suggestion on a change here?
